name: Botswana
summary_text: Botswana is workable for trans visitors — Africa's strongest judicial record after South Africa. The High Court decriminalised same-sex conduct in 2019 (Letsweletse Motshidiemang v AG, upheld 2021); the Court of Appeal ordered the government to register LEGABIBO; and trans people have won document-change cases (ND v Attorney General, 2017). Draft 2024 constitutional changes even contemplate intersex rights. Implementation lags the rulings (SALC documents unsatisfactory compliance), social conservatism persists, and there is no general LGR statute — but the courts are a genuine protection, unique in the region. For a visitor: decriminalised, functioning courts, moderate social hostility.

sources.title: To comply or not to comply is not the question - Southern Africa Litigation Centre
sources.claim_summary: SALC article (May 2024) by Daniel Digashu and Anna Mmolai-Chalmers: courts in Botswana and Namibia have issued landmark LGBTQI+ rulings (Botswana: LEGABIBO registration ordered 2016; 2019 High Court decriminalisation upheld on appeal 2021), but implementation of the orders has been unsatisfactory - governments slow to comply.

sources.title: Botswana: Draft constitutional changes include intersex rights - but other challenges remain
sources.claim_summary: Alta Advisory (June 2024): Botswana's proposed constitutional change would protect intersex rights - analysis of the reform process.

sources.title: Outcome Report >> Botswana, Review Documentation, 43rd Session, May 2023 | UPR Database
sources.claim_summary: UN UPR outcome report for Botswana (43rd session, May 2023): recommendations to repeal Section 167 of the Penal Code (criminalising same-sex conduct for women) and to introduce a clear administrative process for legal gender recognition did not enjoy Botswana's support; same-sex relations between women remain criminalised and no LGR process exists.

US State Department 2011 Human Rights Report for Botswana: general human-rights assessment (violence against women, prison conditions, San discrimination) - the LGBT section documents the then-criminalised status and societal discrimination.

sources.title: LEGABIBO – The Lesbians, Gays & Bisexuals of Botswana
sources.claim_summary: LEGABIBO (Lesbians, Gays & Bisexuals of Botswana) official blog: the organisation's activities - World AIDS Day commemorations, HIV stigma work, Pan Africa ILGA conference participation - documenting the community organisation's operations after winning its registration battle.

sources.title: Botswana to recognise a transgender woman’s identity for first time after historic High Court ruling | The Independent | The Independent
sources.claim_summary: The Independent (Dec 2017): Botswana's High Court ordered the government to legally recognise a trans woman's gender for the first time - Tshepo Ricki Kgositau (director of Gender Dynamix) will receive a female ID card after a four-year legal battle; a landmark for trans rights in Botswana.

sources.title: For LGBT Rights, 2018 Will Be the Year of the Courts | Human Rights Watch
sources.claim_summary: Human Rights Watch (Jan 2018): 'For LGBT Rights, 2018 Will Be the Year of the Courts' — names Botswana's decriminalisation case among the year's key litigation fronts.
